primitives.name: Pretraining Paradigm
primitives.verbatim_quote: We have shifted from training specialized systems from scratch using a large amount of labeled data to a new paradigm of using large-scale pre-training to obtain foundation models, which are then fine-tuned, aligned, and prompted.
primitives.assumptions: Model capacity scales with training data; task universality emerges post-pretraining.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure when data distribution shifts beyond pretraining domain.

primitives.name: Foundation Model Universality

reasoning_traces.think:
The emergence of large language models represents a paradigm shift from supervised learning to self-supervised pretraining. The core idea is that language and world knowledge can be encoded in massive neural networks trained on unlabeled text corpora. This enables a universal model capable of solving diverse downstream tasks through fine-tuning or prompting. The mathematical foundation lies in maximizing likelihood over token sequences, where each token's probability depends on its context. Asymptotically, increasing model size and data volume leads to improved generalization. However, this approach suffers from brittleness under distributional shifts and lacks explicit causal reasoning. Dualities arise between representation learning and compression, where models must balance expressiveness and efficiency. Failure modes include hallucination, overfitting to training data, and inability to reason about novel situations without sufficient exposure during pretraining.
